main_text.p: ftri in l.pen.& vlt.D.de iuftit.& iur,

Quid? Ambiguitatis verborum tractatio cur potius ad Dialecticos, quàm ad Grammaticos pertinet? Quia soli Dialectici vitádæ ambiguitatis artem tradunt, & Sophistis opponuntur, quorum instrumentum omne in ambiguitate & amphibolia positum eft. Nam & multæ fimiles res difsimilibus verbis, & multæ rursus difsimiles fimilibus notatæ funt.Itaque Cicero lib.de Orat.ıı, Ambiguorum(inquit) verborum complura genera funt, quæ mihi videntur melius noffe,qui Dialecticiappellantur.

Velim igitur aliquanto dilucidius bipartitam illam dictionis[?] diuifionem explices. Rerum omnium aliæ ratione & nomine inter fe conueniunt:(Rationem autem appello quam Ariftoteles λόγον τῆς οὐσίας nominat,ideft definitionem qua quid res fit tantùm, non etiá qualis res fit exponitur) vt bos & equus: quorum vterque & definitur & appellatur animal.hæc Dialectici συνώνυμα nominant.aliæ & ratione & nomine inter fe differunt,vt equus, argétum, quorum aliud animal eft, aliud nó animal eft, fed metallũ.Aliæ ratione conueniunt,nomine difcrepant. de quibus hoc Ciceronis exemplum ex Tufcul.ı ıı.exponemus.Sed ratio(inquit) vna omnium eit ægritudinum, plura nomina.Nam & inuidere ægritudinis eft,& ç-mulari,& obtrectare,& misereri,angi,lugere. hæc omnia definiunt Stoici, eáque verba quæ

page.notes: The first line is a fragment continuing from the previous page and is kept as a fragment. "ambiguitatis" is split across a line end with no printed hyphen, so it is written whole. "Grammaticos" is likewise split at a line end without a visible hyphen. "dictionis" is uncertain: the ct ligature is hard to read, so it is marked [?]. "ç-mulari" at the line end is printed as ç with a hyphen; it looks like a misprint for æ and is left as printed. Greek is transcribed as it appears on the scan, with no guarantee of accents or breathings.
